new_categories.label: vessel_legal_registry_identity_state
new_categories.memory: A vessel can have a legal registration/flag identity state that is structurally distinct from its class status, delegated statutory survey state and port-state inspection state. Exact registry law, eligibility and legal consequences require Evidence.

new_categories.label: registered_owner_vs_economic_control_role_separation
new_categories.memory: The entity recorded as registered owner need not be treated as synonymous with the party bearing ultimate economic interest or exercising commercial control. The exact relationship is jurisdiction- and structure-specific and cannot be inferred for named vessels from Memory.

new_categories.label: technical_vs_commercial_management_role_separation
new_categories.memory: Ship operation can be institutionally split between technical management and commercial employment/chartering management, rather than represented as one generic owner/operator role. Exact contracts and responsibilities require Evidence.

new_categories.label: registry_identity_transition_trajectory
new_categories.memory: Registration/flag identity can change over a vessel life, so historical reconstruction should preserve transitions and their known-time rather than treating registry identity as timeless metadata. Exact change mechanics and effective dates require Evidence.

new_categories.label: ownership_control_management_handover_trajectory
new_categories.memory: Sale, financing distress, lease/charter restructuring or manager replacement can produce ownership/control/management handovers on different clocks. A trajectory should not assume all identity layers change together.

new_categories.label: registry_identity_cross_interface_confidence
new_categories.memory: Research may need a bounded confidence state for whether registry, owner/control and manager identities are mutually consistent across historical representations, without using inconsistency itself as proof of wrongdoing or legal defect.

new_categories.label: private_regional_identity_layer_visibility_gap
new_categories.memory: Private/regional fleets may be harder to reconstruct when public-company narratives collapse registered owner, beneficial interest and management identities. This is a source-discovery/representation gap, not a claim about opacity of any named actor.

useful_refinements.label: flag_state_delegation_vs_registry_identity_boundary
useful_refinements.memory: P063 already covers flag delegation to class/recognized organizations; P141 narrows the distinct question to the vessel's legal registration/flag identity rather than delegated survey/certification work.

useful_refinements.label: flag_performance_vs_PSC_boundary
useful_refinements.memory: P064 may use flag/company/class performance as PSC targeting context; that does not make PSC the owner of registry identity or ownership/management relationships.

useful_refinements.label: crew_management_as_role_separation_refinement
useful_refinements.memory: Crew-management separation can matter institutionally, but labor/crewing substance belongs to the already covered workforce family; P141 retains only the ownership/management role boundary.

useful_refinements.label: private_regional_topology_identity_refinement
useful_refinements.memory: P137 owns broad private/regional institutional-service topology. P141 refines that topology only where vessel legal identity and management roles differ from service-provider roles.

useful_refinements.label: identity_transition_not_legal_causality
useful_refinements.memory: Temporal co-movement between registry, ownership or management changes does not establish legal causality, sanctions evasion, tax motive, compliance failure or beneficial ownership.

duplicates.label: classification_and_statutory_survey_status
duplicates.memory: Already covered by P063; class status and delegated statutory work remain separate from registry identity.

duplicates.label: generic_crewing_workforce_state
duplicates.memory: Already covered by dedicated labor/crewing families summarized by P139.

duplicates.label: named_registry_flag_owner_manager_enumeration
duplicates.memory: Named current or historical entity enumeration would drift into source archaeology rather than answer the structural probe.

duplicates.label: generic_owner_operator_role
duplicates.memory: The useful residue is role separation; repeating a generic owner/operator actor category adds little.

reviewed_no_specific_memory: exact flag-state, registry, open/second/international registry, bareboat or dual-registration law and historical effective dates
exact registered-owner, beneficial-owner, mortgagee, lessor, charterer, technical-manager, commercial-manager or crew-manager relationships for named vessels or fleets
exact tonnage-tax, finance, mortgage, sanctions, insurance, chartering, crewing, compliance or tax consequences of registry choice
named private/regional/non-English registry, ownership and management lineages and current status
exact ISM/recognized-organization/delegation responsibilities where legal scope matters
negative_space: claim-scoped reconstruction of registry and ownership/control transitions
exact legal and contractual boundaries among owner, charterer and managers
known-time of identity changes versus later database corrections
stop_reason: The bounded structural questions are answered: legal registry identity, ownership/control separation, technical/commercial management separation and their transition trajectories survive as distinct Memory categories, while class/statutory, PSC, crewing and local-service content collapses to existing families. Remaining detail is exact legal or named-entity source archaeology/Evidence.
epistemic_boundary: Memory-only structural orientation. No named vessel/company/registry ownership, control, management, tax, sanctions, compliance, legal-status or current-state fact is established; no legal or operational advice.
